problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(-4,-5),(0,2),(1,-2).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under a counterclockwise rotation of $\frac{\pi }{4}$ radians about the origin?

- $(-\sqrt{2},\sqrt{2})$
- $(1,-9)$
- $(3,-1)$
worked_solution:
The rotation matrix ${R}_{\theta }$ represents a rotation of angle $\theta $ counterclockwise about the origin and is given by

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}].
$$

Substituting $\theta =\frac{\pi }{4}$ into the above, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}R & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the transformation, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & 1 \\ -5 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the rotation $R$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & 1 \\ -5 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ -9 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\sqrt{2} & \frac{3}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{9}{\sqrt{2}} & \sqrt{2} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are 

$$
(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},-\frac{9}{\sqrt{2}}),\,(-\sqrt{2},\sqrt{2}),\,(\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}},-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}).
$$

So, the correct answer is "I only."
